title: Real-Time Cold-Start Fraud Detection for New Merchant Onboarding using Meta-Learning and Transaction Graph Priors
goal: Score newly registered merchants for fraud risk even with zero transaction history, using graph relationships (shared bank/device/IP) as a prior and an optional meta-learning experiment.
instructions_for_agent: Build phase by phase. Finish and test each phase before starting the next.
Use only synthetic data in phase 1. Never use real bank or identity data.
Shared device/IP/bank alone must NOT define a fraud label. Add noise and legitimate sharing (families, offices).
Split train/test by time and by fraud ring so the same ring never appears in both.
Report PR-AUC, precision, recall, F1. Never report accuracy alone.
Write clear comments and a README explaining every file.

data_plan.primary: Synthetic merchant onboarding dataset generated by src/generate_data.py (no download needed).
optional_public_datasets: IEEE-CIS Fraud Detection (Kaggle) for a separate transaction-model experiment
data_plan.rule: Do not merge public datasets with synthetic merchants. Treat them as separate experiments.

scenarios_to_simulate: fraudster mimicking a genuine merchant (hard case)
genuine merchants sharing an office IP or family device (noise)

phases.name: Data generation
tasks: Create src/generate_data.py producing data/synthetic/merchants.csv and data/synthetic/relationships.csv
Run basic EDA: class balance, missing values, category distribution
phases.done_when: CSV files exist and fraud rate is close to 5 percent

phases.name: Baseline model
tasks: Train Logistic Regression and XGBoost on tabular features only
Use time-based split; handle imbalance with scale_pos_weight
Save metrics to data/processed/baseline_metrics.json
phases.done_when: PR-AUC, precision, recall, F1 are saved

phases.name: Graph features (main innovation)
tasks: Build a NetworkX graph: merchants linked to bank, device, IP, phone
Compute: bank_share_count, device_share_count, ip_share_count, connected_component_size, neighbours_flagged_fraud, louvain_community_fraud_rate
Use only information available before each merchant's registration date (no future leakage)
Retrain XGBoost with graph features and compare to baseline
phases.done_when: Comparison table: baseline vs baseline + graph, especially for merchants with transaction_count = 0

phases.name: Risk engine and explanation
tasks: Calibrate probabilities (isotonic or Platt)
Map score to Approve / Review / Hold using configurable thresholds
Generate SHAP top reasons and the graph evidence path for each flagged merchant
phases.done_when: Each merchant has risk_score, decision, and reasons

phases.name: Flask API and MySQL
tasks: Create database/schema.sql: merchants, relationships, risk_assessments, alerts
Endpoints: POST /api/merchant/register, POST /api/fraud/predict, GET /api/risk/<id>, GET /api/graph/<id>, GET /api/alerts
Save every assessment with model version and timestamp
phases.done_when: Postman or pytest tests pass for all endpoints

phases.name: Power BI export
tasks: Create src/export_for_powerbi.py that writes CSVs into data/powerbi_exports/
Files: merchants_scored.csv, risk_assessments.csv, graph_edges.csv, model_metrics.csv, daily_registrations.csv, alerts.csv
phases.done_when: All CSVs open cleanly in Power BI Desktop

phases.name: Meta-learning (optional experiment)
tasks: Treat each business category as a task with support and query sets
Implement MAML in PyTorch, hold out one category as unseen
Compare against the XGBoost baseline honestly, even if MAML does not win
phases.done_when: Few-shot results table with 5, 10, 20 support examples

powerbi_dashboard.data_sources: CSV files in data/powerbi_exports/ (Get Data > Text/CSV), or MySQL connector for live data

pages.name: Overview
visuals: Cards: total merchants, high-risk count, alerts

pages.name: Risk Analysis
visuals: Table: merchant, risk_score, decision, top reason
Bar chart: average risk by business category

pages.name: Fraud Network
visuals: Network or Decomposition Tree visual from graph_edges.csv

pages.name: Model Performance
visuals: Table: baseline vs graph model (PR-AUC, precision, recall, F1)

new_data_ingestion.goal: The system must work on the preloaded synthetic data AND on new merchant data supplied later by a company, using the same pipeline.

input_contract.note: fraud_label is optional. If present it is used for evaluation or retraining; if absent the system only scores.

ways_to_provide_data: Upload CSV through POST /api/data/upload (file field: merchants_csv)
Send one merchant as JSON through POST /api/merchant/register
Drop a CSV into data/incoming/ and run python src/process_new_data.py
pipeline_steps: 1. Validate: check required columns, data types, duplicates, invalid emails/phones; reject or flag bad rows and report a data_completeness percentage
2. Fill missing optional columns with safe defaults and mark them as 'missing' (missing information is not fraud evidence)
3. Add new entities (banks, devices, IPs) to the existing graph, keeping old data
4. Recompute graph features only from information available at each merchant's registration date
5. Score with the saved model (models/xgb_graph.pkl); no retraining needed for scoring
6. Save risk_score, decision, reasons, model_version, timestamp to MySQL
7. Re-export CSVs to data/powerbi_exports/ so Power BI refresh shows the new merchants
new_data_ingestion.retraining: Provide src/retrain.py. Run it only when new labelled data (fraud_label) is available. Version the model files and keep the old one.
safeguards: Never overwrite the preloaded dataset; store company data in a separate source column (data_source = 'synthetic' or 'company')
If the model or graph fails, send the merchant to manual review instead of auto-approving
Log every upload (who, when, row count, rejected rows)
Do not store real bank credentials; only tokenised or hashed IDs
tests: Upload a CSV with missing optional columns and confirm it still scores
Upload a CSV with a bank account already used by a known fraud merchant and confirm a high graph risk
Upload a CSV with a wrong column name and confirm a clear error message

evaluation.special_test: Evaluate separately on merchants with zero transactions (the cold-start group).

first_prompt_to_agent: Read this spec. Start with Phase 1 only: create the folder structure, requirements.txt, and src/generate_data.py. Run it, show me the first 5 rows of each CSV and the fraud rate, then wait for my approval before Phase 2.
